text: Fixture Bank Limited — Programme Gap Report
What this report states, and what it does not
NO COVERAGE FIGURE APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THIS DOCUMENT. Not a percentage, not a fraction, not a ratio of
dimensions addressed. The pillar hop reaches too much and too indiscriminately to support one: eight leaf dimensions across all
four frameworks reach exactly the same items and the same artefacts, so an answer that looks specific to a dimension is not.
This report says only where the programme has NOTHING, which is a statement about a single pillar and needs no join to be
THE PILLAR IS A FILING, NOT EVIDENCE. A checklist item and a register artefact each carry a pillarId, and that field records
which pillar OWNS the work — nothing more. It carries no weight and no rationale. The crosswalk entry carries both: a
coverageWeight summing to 1.00 across each dimension and an authored sentence saying why the mapping holds. NO
DATASET IN THIS WORKBENCH RELATES A CHECKLIST ITEM OR AN ARTEFACT TO A FRAMEWORK DIMENSION.
Nothing below says that any item addresses any dimension, and reading it that way would compose the weaker edge with the
stronger one and report the result as the stronger.
THREE STATES PER PILLAR, AND NONE OF THEM IS ZERO. HAS A GENERATOR means at least one catalogued artefact
this workbench can produce. NONE BUILT means entries are catalogued and not one may have a generator written for it. NOT
CATALOGUED means the register names this pillar nowhere at all. An unscheduled pillar and a pillar scheduled at zero are
different findings; nothing here lets them print the same, and no pillar is omitted from the table for having nothing.
A WITHDRAWN OR BLOCKED ENTRY IS NOT A REMEDY. Every artefact counted below is printed with its register disposition.
`derived` is the only one a generator may legally be written for; `authored` is library content nobody has written, `observed` is
measured at the client, `blocked` waits on another catalogued artefact, and `withdrawn` was retired with its reason kept. A pillar
showing three catalogued artefacts may have none that this workbench can produce, and P06 is exactly that.
NO ARTEFACT IS ATTACHED TO A WAVE. The waves carry pillar ids and free-text deliverables and no artefact id: of 35
real key, and names no artefact on any wave row.
Layer scope of every figure in this document
Core chassis + banking overlay — every record in all five datasets is in scope.

What each framework puts on each pillar
Structural emphasis from the crosswalk alone, before any answer is given.
THE FOUR FRAMEWORK COLUMNS ARE NOT ADDED TOGETHER. Each is that framework's own structural emphasis —
the share of its view that lands on this pillar if everything were measured — and each column sums to 1.000 down the page.
Adding across a row would weight DGI three times as heavily as DMBOK2, because DGI's ten leaf dimensions sit under three
groups and its raw weights total 3.00 against DMBOK2's 1.00. No dataset defines a weighting across frameworks, so no
A 0.0% column entry means that framework maps nothing to that pillar under this layer. That is a fact about the crosswalk, not a score, and it is
not a gap in the programme.

Pillars with nothing this workbench can produce
A WITHDRAWN OR BLOCKED ENTRY IS NOT A REMEDY. Every artefact counted below is printed with its register disposition.
`derived` is the only one a generator may legally be written for; `authored` is library content nobody has written, `observed` is
measured at the client, `blocked` waits on another catalogued artefact, and `withdrawn` was retired with its reason kept. A pillar
showing three catalogued artefacts may have none that this workbench can produce, and P06 is exactly that.
P06 · Master & Reference Data — NONE BUILT
Single trusted versions of the entities that appear everywhere — customer, product, organisation unit, and the code sets that classify them.
Reference-data drift is the quiet cause of most cross-system inconsistency.
DM08 — these reach this pillar and no other, so nothing else in the programme stands behind them
Golden record definition and match rules
AR-32 (withdrawn) — WITHDRAWN, D5 stage G. The apparent path is the party-domain elements plus the seven Uniqueness rules read as match keys.
Survivorship precedence, match attributes and thresholds have no source in any dataset, and match rules invented under this heading would run against a customer
master. Re-catalogue it when survivorship is authored, not before.
AR-33 (blocked) — BLOCKED, D5 stage G, previously buildable-looking. The apparent path is a regex over dqRules.expression, which yields nine ref_* table names
and five inline enums and looks like a code-set register. It carries no code values, no owner, no versioning and no change process — which is the entire content of
the artefact. The sets live in the client's reference data service and the catalogue harvest is what surfaces them. P06 IS THE LEAST-INSTRUMENTED PILLAR IN
THE MODULE AND THIS ENTRY IS HALF OF THE EVIDENCE: P06 Master & Reference Data holds 0 of the 52 checklist items, has no built artefact, and its only
two register entries are this one and AR-32, which is withdrawn — while waves W2 and W4 both name it. Every other pillar carries at least one checklist item. Visible
only by reading the sequence against the register, which is why it is recorded here rather than left to be noticed.
AR-39 (observed) — The actual group and related-party links. The element that would carry them is catalogued; the linkages themselves are client data.
P09 · Data Lifecycle & Retention — NONE BUILT
Governs data from creation through archival and defensible disposal, including the retention obligations that conflict with deletion rights and the
storage cost of keeping everything forever.
APO14.09 — these reach this pillar and no other, so nothing else in the programme stands behind them
Fixture Bank Limited — Programme Gap Report
AR-19 (authored) — Statutory periods per record category with legal basis. One element carries fsdmEntity 'Retention Rule', which records that retention rules are
data — not what any of them say.
P08 · Security, Privacy & Classification — NONE BUILT
Classification of data by sensitivity, the access model that enforces it, and the privacy obligations attached. This pillar has become the gating
DM05 — these reach this pillar and no other, so nothing else in the programme stands behind them
AR-15 (authored) — Labels and handling rules, authored once. criticality is CRITICAL or HIGH — business impact, not confidentiality — and labelling elements from
it would be the two-vocabularies error at the level of the value rather than the join.
AR-43 (observed) — Entitlement review results. Two Access-family rules exist; the recertification evidence is IAM output.
AR-50 (observed) — CATALOGUED FROM THE SEQUENCE: CL-30 names it and nothing carried it. A constraint per element is a Compliance determination made
from the client's own legal position, not library content. THE APPARENT PATH IS CDE-010 'Customer Residency & Domicile' and CDE-061 'Party Address' —
elements ABOUT residency and jurisdiction, which is not the same as a transfer or confidentiality constraint attached to an element, exactly as AR-19's 'Retention
Rule' entity records that retention rules are data without recording what any of them say. The confidentiality half additionally needs AR-15's label vocabulary before it
AR-52 (blocked) — CATALOGUED FROM THE SEQUENCE: CL-37 requires classification applied and recorded against every governed CDE, as a blocking Platform
item, and no entry existed. Genuinely derivable once AR-15's labels exist and are attached — the denominator is already the governed CDE set under the layer filter
and the three states apply unchanged, labelled / not-labelled / not-applicable, never a zero. It must NOT be derived from cdeRegister.criticality: CRITICAL and HIGH
are business impact, not confidentiality, which is the two-vocabularies error at the level of the value that AR-15's own note fences off.

Waves naming a pillar with nothing scheduled
Wave to pillar only. No artefact is named on any row.
NO ARTEFACT IS ATTACHED TO A WAVE. The waves carry pillar ids and free-text deliverables and no artefact id: of 35
real key, and names no artefact on any wave row.
A wave naming a pillar with nothing built is not necessarily a defect in the plan: the wave may be delivered by hand, and the register catalogues
what a consultant produces rather than only what this workbench generates. It is a place where the plan and the generated pack do not meet,
and where a client asking "what will you hand me for this?" has no answer from this tool.
